claims.text: The investigated alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy initially has a single-phase BCC structure.
The constituent elements are homogeneously distributed before loading.
Finely dispersed coherent nanoprecipitates form in WTaTiVZr during or before high-temperature deformation.
The coherent nanoprecipitates are embedded within a BCC matrix.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve local stress concentrations.
Coherent precipitate interfaces lower the energy barrier for dislocation movement.
Nanoprecipitate-mediated dislocation behavior promotes multistage or progressive strain hardening.
Relieving stress concentrations delays premature crack initiation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates are the primary cause of enhanced plastic strain and toughness in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
At 800°C and above, WTaTiVZr will have greater tensile strain-to-failure than commercially pure tungsten tested identically.
At 800°C and above, WTaTiVZr will have greater toughness or energy absorption than commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit a delayed onset of plastic instability relative to pure tungsten.
Commercially pure tungsten has limited plastic strain and toughness under the specified elevated-temperature conditions because of inherent brittleness.
Temperatures of approximately 800°C and above are relevant to high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
The proposed mechanism operates only while the nanoprecipitates remain stable and coherent at service temperature.
The WTaVTiZrx alloy system can retain its overall microstructure after annealing at 900°C for 5–10 hours.
Testing WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten at identical temperature, strain rate, and atmosphere provides a controlled performance comparison.
Failure to observe both improved mechanical performance and coherent nanoprecipitates would falsify the proposed nanoprecipitate mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as compositionally homogeneous and single-phase before loading, while the mediator is allowed to consist of nanoprecipitates already present prior to loading. Pre-existing chemically or structurally distinct precipitates would conflict with the stated homogeneous single-phase initial state unless 'single phase' refers only to the matrix or the precipitates form during loading.
